people.name: Katsushika Hokusai
people.why: The Great Wave off Kanagawa is probably the most reproduced image in Japanese art.

people.name: Murasaki Shikibu
people.why: The Tale of Genji, written by a court lady a thousand years ago, is often called the first novel.

people.name: Akira Kurosawa
people.why: Seven Samurai and Rashomon reshaped world cinema; Hollywood remade both.

people.name: Hayao Miyazaki
people.why: Spirited Away won an Oscar and made Studio Ghibli a household name worldwide.

people.name: Shigeru Miyamoto
people.why: Created Mario and Zelda, and much of the grammar of modern video games.

events.title: The Edo period
events.what: Two and a half centuries of near-total isolation under the Tokugawa shoguns, and of extraordinary urban culture.

events.title: The Meiji Restoration
events.what: Ended shogun rule and industrialised Japan at a speed nobody thought possible.

events.title: Hiroshima and Nagasaki
events.what: The only use of nuclear weapons in war; Japan's postwar constitution renounces war outright.

events.title: The Tokyo Olympics
events.what: The bullet train opened days before, and Japan announced its postwar recovery to the world.

culture.label: Greeting
culture.text: A bow rather than a handshake; the deeper and longer, the more respect.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Washoku is UNESCO-listed. Regional specialities matter enormously, and slurping noodles is correct.

culture.label: Onsen
culture.text: Hot-spring bathing, naked, after washing thoroughly first — a national pastime with strict etiquette.

culture.label: Seasons
culture.text: Cherry blossom, autumn leaves and seasonal food are followed closely and forecast on the news.

culture.label: Manner
culture.text: Quiet in public, no eating while walking, and a strong preference for not imposing on others.

talkAbout: Food, and the speciality of their home region.
Where they're from — Tokyo, Kansai and Kyushu are genuinely different.
Seasonal festivals and where to see blossom.
avoid: The Second World War, especially Japan's actions in Asia, is difficult ground. Don't stick chopsticks upright in rice — it echoes a funeral rite.

people.name: Confucius
people.why: His ethics of family, duty and learning shaped East Asian society for two millennia.

people.name: Qin Shi Huang
people.why: Unified China, standardised its script, and was buried with the Terracotta Army.

people.name: Tu Youyou
people.why: Found artemisinin in a fourth-century text and saved millions of lives from malaria; Nobel, 2015.

people.name: Li Bai
people.why: The most beloved poet in the language; Chinese schoolchildren still memorise his verses.

people.name: Zheng He
people.why: Led treasure fleets to Africa decades before Columbus, in ships several times larger.

events.title: Unification
events.what: The Qin state unified the warring kingdoms and created the idea of a single China.

events.title: The Tang dynasty
events.what: A cosmopolitan golden age of poetry, trade along the Silk Road, and the world's largest city at Chang'an.

events.title: The century of humiliation
events.what: The Opium Wars, foreign concessions and invasion — the framing through which much of modern policy is explained.

events.title: Reform and opening
events.what: Deng Xiaoping's reforms began the fastest lift out of poverty in human history.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Eight great regional cuisines; Sichuan and Cantonese cooking have almost nothing in common.

culture.label: Spring Festival
culture.text: Lunar New Year produces the largest annual human migration on earth.

culture.label: Family
culture.text: Filial duty is a live obligation, and elders are addressed by relationship terms rather than names.

culture.label: Tea
culture.text: Tea culture is regional and ritualised; pouring for others before yourself is basic courtesy.

culture.label: Face
culture.text: Mianzi — social standing — shapes how disagreement, refusal and praise are expressed.

talkAbout: Food, and their province's cuisine.
Family and where they go for Spring Festival.
History, poetry and calligraphy.
avoid: Taiwan, Tibet, Xinjiang, Hong Kong and 1989 are politically dangerous subjects. Don't assume anyone's views from their nationality.

people.name: Mahatma Gandhi
people.why: Made non-violent resistance a tool that ended an empire, and a model copied worldwide.

people.name: B. R. Ambedkar
people.why: Born Dalit, he wrote India's constitution and led the fight against caste discrimination.

people.name: Rabindranath Tagore
people.why: The first non-European to win the Nobel in Literature; wrote two national anthems.

people.name: Srinivasa Ramanujan
people.why: Largely self-taught, he produced results mathematicians are still working through.

people.name: Lata Mangeshkar
people.why: Recorded for Hindi cinema across seven decades and was its defining voice.

events.title: The Indus Valley civilisation
events.what: Cities with drainage and standardised bricks, and a script still undeciphered.

events.title: The Mughal Empire
events.what: Built the Taj Mahal and much of north India's architecture, cuisine and court culture.

events.title: Independence and Partition
events.what: Freedom from Britain came with a division that displaced 15 million people and killed perhaps a million.

events.title: Liberalisation
events.what: Economic reforms opened the economy and set off three decades of growth.

culture.label: Namaste
culture.text: Palms together at chest height. A handshake is fine, but not always between men and women.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Utterly regional — a Kerala meal and a Punjabi one share almost nothing. Eating with the right hand is normal.

culture.label: Festivals
culture.text: Diwali, Holi, Eid, Christmas, Pongal and many more; the calendar is crowded.

culture.label: Languages
culture.text: 22 scheduled languages and hundreds more; many Indians speak three or four.

culture.label: Cinema
culture.text: The world's largest film industry by output, and 'Bollywood' is only the Hindi part of it.

talkAbout: Which state they're from, and its food and language.
Cricket — it is closer to a national religion than a sport.
Films and music, regional as much as Hindi.
avoid: Caste, religion and Pakistan are all sensitive. Don't treat India as culturally uniform, and don't assume everyone is vegetarian or Hindu.

people.name: Sukarno
people.why: Declared independence in 1945 and led the Non-Aligned Movement from Bandung.

people.name: Raden Ajeng Kartini
people.why: Her letters on women's education became the founding text of Indonesian feminism; her birthday is a national day.

people.name: Pramoedya Ananta Toer
people.why: Wrote the Buru Quartet in a prison camp, dictating it to fellow inmates before he had paper.

people.name: Susi Susanti
people.why: Won Indonesia's first Olympic gold in 1992 and is a national icon.

people.name: B. J. Habibie
people.why: An aeronautical engineer with patents to his name who oversaw the transition to democracy.

events.title: Borobudur built
events.what: The largest Buddhist temple in the world, on Java, later abandoned and reclaimed by jungle.

events.title: Dutch rule
events.what: Three and a half centuries of colonial control, first by a company and then by the state.

events.title: Independence declared
events.what: Sukarno proclaimed independence days after Japan's surrender; four years of war followed.

events.title: Reformasi
events.what: Suharto resigned after 31 years, opening Indonesia's democratic era.

culture.label: Scale
culture.text: Over 17,000 islands, 1,300 ethnic groups and 700 languages, held together by one national language.

culture.label: Wayang
culture.text: Shadow puppetry with all-night performances of the Ramayana, UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Batik
culture.text: Wax-resist cloth with regional patterns, worn to work and to weddings alike.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Nasi goreng, rendang, satay and sambal; heat and sweetness together.

culture.label: Gotong royong
culture.text: Mutual help — communities still turn out together for building, cleaning and ceremonies.

talkAbout: Which island they're from and what makes it different.
Food, especially rendang and regional sambals.
Badminton, which Indonesia dominates.
avoid: Papua, the 1965–66 killings and religious politics are sensitive. Use the right hand for giving and eating.

people.name: King Sejong
people.why: Invented Hangul so ordinary people could read; it is now considered a model writing system.

people.name: Yi Sun-sin
people.why: Won 23 naval battles without losing one, including against odds of 13 ships to over 100.

people.name: Bong Joon-ho
people.why: Parasite was the first non-English film to win Best Picture at the Oscars.

people.name: Kim Dae-jung
people.why: Survived a kidnapping and a death sentence as a dissident, then won the Nobel Peace Prize.

people.name: Nam June Paik
people.why: Invented video art, and predicted the 'electronic superhighway' in 1974.

events.title: Hangul created
events.what: A phonetic alphabet designed so that 'a wise man can learn it in a morning'.

events.title: Japanese occupation
events.what: Thirty-five years of colonial rule that suppressed the language and remains a live diplomatic issue.

events.title: The Korean War
events.what: Millions died and the peninsula was divided by an armistice — not a peace treaty — still in force.

events.title: Democratisation
events.what: Mass protests forced direct presidential elections and ended military rule.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Kimchi at every meal, banchan side dishes covering the table, and barbecue cooked at it.

culture.label: Hierarchy
culture.text: Age determines speech level and seating; people ask your age early for exactly this reason.

culture.label: Hallyu
culture.text: K-pop, K-drama and Korean film went from national to global in about twenty years.

culture.label: Drinking
culture.text: Pour for others, never yourself; turn away from elders when you drink.

culture.label: Hiking
culture.text: Mountains cover most of the country and hiking, fully kitted out, is a national habit.

talkAbout: Food, and whether they make their own kimchi.
Film and music.
Hiking and which mountain they climbed last.
avoid: Japan's colonial period, North Korea and regional politics are sensitive. Don't write someone's name in red ink.

people.name: King Bhumibol Adulyadej
people.native: ภูมิพลอดุลยเดช
people.why: Reigned 70 years, the longest of any Thai king, and is deeply revered.

people.name: King Chulalongkorn
people.native: จุฬาลงกรณ์
people.why: Abolished slavery and modernised Siam, keeping it the only Southeast Asian state never colonised.

people.name: Apichatpong Weerasethakul
people.why: Won the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 2010 with Uncle Boonmee.

people.name: Buakaw Banchamek
people.why: The sport's best-known international name and a major reason for its global spread.

people.name: Sunthorn Phu
people.why: Thailand's greatest poet, whose Phra Aphai Mani is a national epic.

events.title: Sukhothai
events.what: The first Thai kingdom, and the source of the Thai script and much of its Buddhist art.

events.title: Bangkok founded
events.what: The Chakri dynasty moved the capital across the river and began the present line of kings.

events.title: Staying independent
events.what: Skilful diplomacy between Britain and France kept Siam the only uncolonised state in the region.

events.title: The end of absolute monarchy
events.what: A bloodless coup made Siam a constitutional monarchy.

culture.label: The wai
culture.text: Palms together with a slight bow; the height of the hands signals the level of respect.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Sour, sweet, salty and hot in every dish, and street food is where the best of it is.

culture.label: Songkran
culture.text: Thai New Year in April, which has become a three-day nationwide water fight.

culture.label: Sanuk & jai yen
culture.text: Enjoyment in whatever you do, and a 'cool heart' — losing your temper loses you respect.

culture.label: Muay Thai
culture.text: The national sport, with a pre-fight dance honouring teachers and family.

talkAbout: Food, and which region's cooking they prefer.
Songkran and Loy Krathong.
Muay Thai and football.
avoid: Criticism of the monarchy is a criminal offence with long sentences. Never touch someone's head or point your feet at people or Buddha images.

people.name: Hồ Chí Minh
people.why: Led the independence struggle against France and then the United States.

people.name: Võ Nguyên Giáp
people.why: A history teacher who defeated the French at Điện Biên Phủ and became one of the century's great commanders.

people.name: The Trưng Sisters
people.why: Drove out Chinese rule and ruled for three years; still the emblem of Vietnamese resistance.

people.name: Nguyễn Du
people.why: The Tale of Kiều is the national poem, and many Vietnamese can quote long passages.

people.name: Đặng Thái Sơn
people.why: The first Asian to win the International Chopin Competition, having practised on a piano in a jungle shelter.

events.title: A thousand years of Chinese rule
events.what: A millennium of domination that Vietnam's identity was partly forged in resisting.

events.title: Điện Biên Phủ
events.what: The defeat that ended French colonial rule in Indochina.

events.title: The war
events.what: Known in Vietnam as the American War; it ended with the fall of Saigon and reunification.

events.title: Đổi Mới
events.what: Market reforms turned one of the world's poorest countries into one of its fastest-growing.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Phở for breakfast, bánh mì from a cart, and herbs by the plateful with everything.

culture.label: Coffee
culture.text: The world's second-largest producer; drip-filtered over condensed milk, or with egg in Hanoi.

culture.label: Motorbikes
culture.text: Tens of millions of them, and crossing the road means walking slowly and steadily.

culture.label: Tết
culture.text: Lunar New Year, when the whole country goes home and everything closes for days.

culture.label: Ancestors
culture.text: Almost every home has an ancestral altar, tended with incense and offerings.

talkAbout: Food and coffee — endlessly rewarding subjects here.
Family and Tết traditions.
The north–south differences in accent and cooking.
avoid: The war is remembered very differently here than in the West. Politics and the party are not open topics with strangers.

people.name: José Rizal
people.why: His novels exposed Spanish colonial abuses; his execution triggered the revolution.

people.name: Corazon Aquino
people.why: A housewife turned leader of the People Power revolution, and Asia's first woman president.

people.name: Manny Pacquiao
people.why: The only boxer to win world titles in eight weight divisions.

people.name: Lapulapu
people.why: Defeated Magellan at Mactan — the first recorded resistance to European colonisation in the islands.

people.name: Lea Salonga
people.why: Won a Tony for Miss Saigon and was the singing voice of two Disney princesses.

events.title: Magellan arrives
events.what: The first European contact; Magellan was killed at Mactan weeks later.

events.title: Spanish rule
events.what: Three centuries that made the Philippines Asia's largest Catholic country.

events.title: American rule
events.what: Followed a brutal war; it left English, a school system and close ties to the United States.

events.title: People Power
events.what: Millions filled EDSA and removed Marcos without a shot; the template for peaceful revolutions since.

culture.label: Family

culture.label: Karaoke
culture.text: A national pastime, in homes, streets and buses, and taken more seriously than you'd expect.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Adobo, sinigang and lechon; Spanish, Chinese, Malay and American influences on one plate.

culture.label: Christmas
culture.text: Decorations go up in September; it is the longest Christmas season in the world.

culture.label: Po and opo
culture.text: Respect particles added when speaking to elders, plus mano — touching an elder's hand to your forehead.

talkAbout: Family, and which province they're from.
Food and karaoke.
Basketball, which is the national obsession.
avoid: The Marcos era and the drug war are deeply divisive. Overseas workers' separation from families is a real hardship, not a light topic.

people.name: Ibn Saud
people.why: United the Arabian peninsula by conquest and founded the modern kingdom in 1932.

people.name: Haifaa al-Mansour
people.why: Directed Wadjda, the first feature film shot entirely in Saudi Arabia, and by a woman.

people.name: Abdul Rahman Al-Sudais
people.why: Imam of the Grand Mosque in Mecca, whose recitation is known to Muslims worldwide.

people.name: Ghazi Al-Gosaibi
people.why: A cabinet minister and ambassador who was also one of the Gulf's leading poets and novelists.

people.name: Hayat Sindi
people.why: A biotechnologist who developed low-cost diagnostics for use without laboratories.

events.title: The life of Muhammad
events.what: Islam began in Mecca and Medina; both cities are in Saudi Arabia and are its defining fact.

events.title: The kingdom founded
events.what: Ibn Saud proclaimed the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia after three decades of campaigning.

events.title: Oil at Dammam
events.what: The discovery that transformed the kingdom and the world's energy economy.

events.title: Vision 2030
events.what: A programme to move the economy off oil, alongside rapid social change including women driving.

culture.label: The Hajj
culture.text: Millions travel to Mecca each year for the pilgrimage every able Muslim is expected to make once.

culture.label: Qahwa
culture.text: Cardamom-spiced coffee with dates, poured by the host; shake the cup gently to signal you've had enough.

culture.label: Hospitality
culture.text: Guests are honoured seriously, and refusing food or coffee outright is difficult.

culture.label: Bedouin heritage
culture.text: Camel racing, falconry and poetry competitions remain genuinely popular.

culture.label: Kabsa
culture.text: Spiced rice with lamb or chicken, eaten from a shared platter with the right hand.

talkAbout: Coffee and dates, and the etiquette around them.
Family and tribe, which people are proud of.
Football, which is followed intensely.
avoid: Religion, the royal family and human rights are not safe conversational ground. Alcohol is illegal, and public behaviour rules are enforced.

people.name: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk
people.why: Built a secular republic from the Ottoman collapse and changed the alphabet, calendar and law.

people.name: Mimar Sinan
people.why: Built over 300 structures for the Ottoman sultans, including the Süleymaniye and Selimiye mosques.

people.name: Orhan Pamuk
people.why: Nobel laureate in 2006, whose novels are built around Istanbul's melancholy.

people.name: Rumi
people.why: Lived and died in Konya; his poetry is among the best-selling in the world today.

people.name: Aziz Sancar
people.why: Won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2015 for mapping how cells repair DNA.

events.title: The conquest of Constantinople
events.what: Mehmed II took the city, ending the Byzantine Empire and making Istanbul an Ottoman capital.

events.title: Süleyman the Magnificent
events.what: The Ottoman Empire at its height, stretching from Hungary to Yemen.

events.title: The Republic
events.what: Atatürk founded a secular republic on the empire's ruins and moved the capital to Ankara.

events.title: The earthquakes
events.what: Two enormous quakes in the south-east killed more than 50,000 people.

culture.label: Çay
culture.text: Black tea in tulip glasses, offered constantly, everywhere, all day.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Kebabs are only the start: mezes, breakfast spreads and a vast pastry tradition.

culture.label: Hospitality
culture.text: Guests are fed and refused permission to pay; arguing over the bill is a genuine contest.

culture.label: Nazar
culture.text: The blue evil-eye bead hangs in homes, cars and on babies' clothes.

culture.label: Hamam
culture.text: The Turkish bath, with scrubbing and foam, is an old and still-living institution.

talkAbout: Food and tea, both inexhaustible.
Football, and the Istanbul club rivalries.
History — Roman, Byzantine, Ottoman, all in the same streets.
avoid: The Armenian genocide, the Kurdish question and Atatürk's legacy are all sensitive; insulting Atatürk is illegal.

people.name: David Ben-Gurion
people.why: Declared Israel's independence in 1948 and led it through its first years.

people.name: Golda Meir
people.why: One of the first women in the world to lead a country, in office during the 1973 war.

people.name: Amos Oz
people.why: One of Hebrew literature's major figures and a lifelong advocate of a two-state solution.

people.name: Daniel Kahneman
people.why: Won the Nobel in economics for work on how people actually make decisions.

people.name: Ada Yonath
people.why: Nobel laureate in chemistry for mapping the structure of the ribosome.

events.title: Zionism and the Mandate
events.what: A movement for a Jewish state, British rule over Palestine, and rising conflict between communities.

events.title: Independence and the Nakba
events.what: Israel declared statehood; war followed, and around 700,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled.

events.title: The Six-Day War
events.what: Israel captured the West Bank, Gaza, Sinai and the Golan, beginning an occupation that continues.

events.title: The Oslo Accords
events.what: Created the Palestinian Authority but left the hardest questions unresolved.

culture.label: Shabbat
culture.text: From Friday sunset to Saturday night much of the country stops; buses and shops close.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Hummus, falafel and shakshuka, drawn from Levantine, North African and Eastern European kitchens.

culture.label: Directness
culture.text: Blunt to the point of abruptness, and not meant unkindly; dugri means talking straight.

culture.label: Conscription
culture.text: Military service is compulsory for most Jewish Israelis, and shapes social life and networks.

culture.label: Diversity
culture.text: Jews from a hundred countries, plus a fifth of citizens who are Arab, with their own communities.

talkAbout: Food, and the arguments about who invented what.
Hiking and the desert.
Technology and startups, a major part of the economy.
avoid: The conflict with the Palestinians is the most contested subject in the world and divides Israelis sharply among themselves. Listen rather than assert.

people.name: Mahmoud Darwish
people.why: The Palestinian national poet, whose verses are recited across the Arab world.

people.name: Edward Said
people.why: Orientalism changed how the West studies the East, and how it sees itself doing so.

people.name: Ghassan Kanafani
people.why: Men in the Sun is the central novella of Palestinian exile; he was assassinated at 36.

people.name: Hanan Ashrawi
people.why: The first woman to hold a seat on the Palestinian National Council's executive, and a leading negotiator.

people.name: Elia Suleiman
people.why: His deadpan, near-silent films have won prizes at Cannes and defined Palestinian cinema.

events.title: The Nakba
events.what: Around 700,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled during the war; most were never allowed to return.

events.title: The occupation begins
events.what: Israel took the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza; military occupation of the West Bank continues.

events.title: The First Intifada
events.what: A mass uprising of strikes, boycotts and stone-throwing that brought Palestinians to the negotiating table.

events.title: UN observer state
events.what: The General Assembly recognised Palestine as a non-member observer state.

culture.label: Tatreez
culture.text: Cross-stitch embroidery whose patterns identify a woman's village; UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Olives
culture.text: The olive harvest each autumn is a family and community event, and the tree is a national symbol.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Musakhan, maqluba served upside down onto the plate, and knafeh from Nablus.

culture.label: Keffiyeh
culture.text: The black-and-white checked scarf is worn as everyday clothing and as a symbol.

culture.label: Dabke
culture.text: A line dance with stamping footwork, performed at every wedding across the Levant.

Poetry and literature — Darwish is known by heart.
Family and where their village or town is.

people.name: Cyrus the Great

people.name: Hafez
people.why: Most Iranian homes have a copy of his poems, opened at random for guidance.

people.name: Ferdowsi
people.why: The Shahnameh saved Persian as a literary language after the Arab conquest.

people.name: Maryam Mirzakhani
people.why: The first woman to win the Fields Medal; she died at 40.

people.name: Abbas Kiarostami
people.why: Won the Palme d'Or and made Iranian cinema one of the most admired in the world.

events.title: The Persian Empire
events.what: The largest empire the world had yet seen, stretching from Egypt to the Indus.

events.title: The Safavids
events.what: Made Shia Islam the state religion, setting Iran apart from its Sunni neighbours ever since.

events.title: The coup
events.what: A British and American operation removed the elected prime minister Mosaddegh after he nationalised oil.

events.title: The Revolution
events.what: The Shah was overthrown and an Islamic Republic established, reshaping regional politics.

culture.label: Nowruz

culture.label: Taarof
culture.text: An elaborate politeness where offers are refused several times before being accepted. Expect it everywhere.

culture.label: Poetry
culture.text: Hafez and Rumi are quoted in ordinary conversation, and their tombs are visited like shrines.

culture.label: Food

culture.label: Carpets
culture.text: Persian carpet weaving is a centuries-old art with regional designs and enormous prestige.

Family and hospitality.

people.name: Malala Yousafzai

people.name: Abdus Salam
people.why: The first Muslim Nobel laureate in science, for unifying two of the fundamental forces.

people.name: Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan
people.why: Took qawwali devotional music to global audiences and is regarded as one of the great voices.

people.name: Benazir Bhutto
people.why: The first woman to lead a Muslim-majority country in modern times; assassinated while campaigning.

events.title: Mohenjo-daro
events.what: One of the Indus Valley's great cities, with grid streets and drainage, in modern Sindh.

events.title: Partition

events.title: Bangladesh secedes
events.what: East Pakistan became Bangladesh after a war of independence.

events.title: Nuclear tests
events.what: Pakistan tested nuclear weapons weeks after India, making South Asia a nuclear region.

culture.label: Cricket

culture.label: Food

culture.label: Qawwali
culture.text: Sufi devotional singing performed at shrines, building over half an hour to something ecstatic.

culture.label: Mountains

culture.label: Hospitality

Food, and which city does which dish best.
The northern mountains, which few outsiders know about.

people.name: Muhammad Yunus

people.name: Kazi Nazrul Islam

people.name: Shakib Al Hasan

culture.label: Bengali
