culture.label: Pohela Boishakh
culture.text: Bengali New Year in April, with a UNESCO-listed procession of giant masks in Dhaka.

culture.label: Sundarbans
culture.text: The world's largest mangrove forest, and home to the Bengal tiger.

culture.label: Dhaka
culture.text: One of the most densely populated cities on earth, and a rickshaw capital.

talkAbout: Language and poetry — Tagore and Nazrul are both loved here.
Cricket — it is closer to a national religion than a sport.
Food, especially fish and sweets.
avoid: The 1971 war and its atrocities are painful; relations with Pakistan and domestic politics are polarised. Garment-factory disasters are a sore point.

people.name: Sheikh Zayed
people.why: United seven emirates in 1971 and is regarded as the father of the country.

people.name: Sheikha Lubna Al Qasimi
people.why: The first woman to hold a cabinet post in the UAE.

people.name: Hazza Al Mansouri
people.why: The first Emirati in space, in 2019.

people.name: Sarah Al Amiri
people.why: Led the science team behind the Hope probe that reached Mars orbit in 2021.

people.name: Ahmed Rashid Thani
people.why: A leading voice in modern Emirati poetry and theatre.

events.title: The Trucial States
events.what: British-protected sheikhdoms along the coast, known for pearling before oil.

events.title: Oil found in Abu Dhabi
events.what: The discovery that funded the transformation of the entire coast.

events.title: The federation
events.what: Six emirates federated on independence, with Ras Al Khaimah joining the following year.

events.title: Hope reaches Mars
events.what: The UAE became the fifth space agency to reach Mars orbit, on its first attempt.

culture.label: Diversity
culture.text: Around 88% of residents are foreign nationals; you will meet people from everywhere.

culture.label: Majlis
culture.text: The sitting room where guests are received and matters discussed; UNESCO-listed as a social practice.

culture.label: Falconry
culture.text: Falcons have their own passports and travel in aircraft cabins.

culture.label: Ramadan
culture.text: Public eating and drinking are avoided in daylight; iftar after sunset is a large social occasion.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Machboos, harees and luqaimat dumplings in date syrup.

talkAbout: Falconry and desert traditions.
The space programme, which Emiratis are genuinely proud of.
Food, and where to find good Emirati cooking, which is harder than it sounds.
avoid: Criticism of the rulers, and questions about migrant labour conditions, are risky. Public displays of affection and drinking outside licensed venues are offences.

people.name: Lee Kuan Yew
people.why: Led Singapore from independence to first-world status in a single generation.

people.name: Joseph Schooling
people.why: Beat Michael Phelps to win Singapore's first Olympic gold in 2016.

people.name: Sonny Liew
people.why: The Art of Charlie Chan Hock Chye won three Eisner Awards and retells Singapore's history sideways.

people.name: Yusof bin Ishak
people.why: Singapore's first head of state, whose face is on every banknote.

people.name: Violet Oon
people.why: Spent decades documenting and defending Peranakan cooking.

events.title: Raffles arrives
events.what: The British East India Company founded a free port that grew into a trading hub.

events.title: The fall of Singapore
events.what: Britain's largest surrender ever, followed by a brutal Japanese occupation.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Expelled from Malaysia, Singapore became a country against its own wishes.

events.title: The transformation
events.what: From GDP per head near Mexico's to among the highest in the world in fifty years.

culture.label: Hawker centres
culture.text: Cheap, excellent food courts that are UNESCO-listed; a packet of tissues on a table reserves it.

culture.label: Singlish
culture.text: English with Malay, Hokkien and Tamil grammar and particles — lah, leh, lor.

culture.label: Four communities
culture.text: Chinese, Malay, Indian and 'Others', with four official languages and everyone's holidays public.

culture.label: City in a garden
culture.text: Deliberate greening since the 1960s; the tree canopy is planned infrastructure.

culture.label: Rules
culture.text: Fines for many things, chewing gum sales restricted, and a general expectation of order.

talkAbout: Food, and which hawker stall is best — this can go on for hours.
Singlish and its particles.
How much the city has changed in a generation.
avoid: Race, religion and free speech are legally sensitive here. 'Fine city' jokes are extremely well worn.

people.name: Tunku Abdul Rahman
people.why: Led Malaya to independence in 1957 and is called the father of the nation.

people.name: Nicol David
people.why: World number one for a record 108 months and eight-time world champion.

people.name: P. Ramlee
people.why: Made 66 films and wrote hundreds of songs; the defining figure of Malay popular culture.

people.name: Yuna
people.why: A singer-songwriter who broke internationally while keeping her Malaysian identity front and centre.

people.name: Lee Chong Wei
people.why: World number one for 349 weeks and three-time Olympic silver medallist.

events.title: The Malacca Sultanate
events.what: A trading port that made Malay the lingua franca of maritime Southeast Asia.

events.title: Merdeka
events.what: Independence from Britain, declared at the Merdeka Stadium in Kuala Lumpur.

events.title: Malaysia formed
events.what: Malaya, Sabah, Sarawak and Singapore federated; Singapore left two years later.

events.title: The first change of government
events.what: Sixty-one years of one coalition's rule ended at the ballot box.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Nasi lemak, laksa and roti canai; mamak stalls stay open all night and everyone goes.

culture.label: Plural society
culture.text: Malay, Chinese and Indian communities with an 'open house' custom at each other's festivals.

culture.label: Two halves
culture.text: Peninsular Malaysia and Borneo, the latter with its own indigenous peoples and rainforest.

culture.label: Badminton
culture.text: The national sport, and the source of most of Malaysia's Olympic medals.

culture.label: Manner
culture.text: Indirect and polite; use the right hand, and take off shoes entering a home.

talkAbout: Food, endlessly, and which state does it best.
Badminton, which Malaysia follows more closely than football.
Borneo, and the difference between the two halves of the country.
avoid: Race-based policy, religion and royalty are legally and socially sensitive. Don't confuse Malaysia with Singapore or Indonesia.

people.name: Tenzing Norgay
people.why: With Edmund Hillary, the first to reach the summit of Everest, in 1953.

people.name: Siddhartha Gautama
people.why: Born at Lumbini in what is now Nepal, and the source of a religion followed by half a billion people.

people.name: Bhanubhakta Acharya
people.why: Translated the Ramayana into Nepali and effectively created its literature.

people.name: Pasang Lhamu Sherpa
people.why: The first Nepali woman to summit Everest; she died on the descent.

people.name: Kami Rita Sherpa
people.why: Has summited Everest more times than anyone in history.

events.title: Unification
events.what: Prithvi Narayan Shah conquered the Kathmandu Valley and built the Nepali state.

events.title: The Anglo-Nepalese War
events.what: Nepal held Britain to a costly draw; the Gurkha regiments date from the peace that followed.

events.title: The civil war
events.what: A Maoist insurgency killed around 17,000 people and ended with the abolition of the monarchy.

events.title: The earthquake
events.what: Nearly 9,000 people died and much of the Kathmandu Valley's heritage was destroyed.

culture.label: Himalaya
culture.text: Eight of the world's ten highest peaks, and a whole economy built around them.

culture.label: Namaste
culture.text: Palms together, and a strong sense of respect for elders and teachers.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Dal bhat twice a day, and momo dumplings that came down from Tibet.

culture.label: Dashain & Tihar
culture.text: Two long autumn festivals; Tihar includes a day of honouring dogs.

culture.label: Coexistence
culture.text: Hindu and Buddhist practice overlap here in ways that are hard to separate.

talkAbout: Trekking, and which routes they'd recommend.
Festivals, especially Dashain and Tihar.
Food, and the difference between hill and Newari cooking.
avoid: Sherpas are an ethnic group, not a job title. The civil war and caste discrimination are difficult subjects.

people.name: Genghis Khan
people.why: Built the largest contiguous land empire in history; he is on the banknotes and the airport.

people.name: Kublai Khan
people.why: Founded the Yuan dynasty in China and received Marco Polo at his court.

people.name: Zanabazar
people.why: The first Bogd Gegeen, and the greatest artist in Mongolian Buddhist sculpture.

people.name: Damdin Sükhbaatar
people.why: Led the 1921 revolution; the main square in Ulaanbaatar carries his name.

people.name: Naidangiin Tüvshinbayar
people.why: Won Mongolia's first Olympic gold medal in 2008.

events.title: The Mongol Empire
events.what: Temüjin was proclaimed Genghis Khan and united the steppe tribes.

events.title: Independence from the Qing
events.what: Mongolia broke away as the Chinese empire collapsed.

events.title: The socialist period
events.what: The world's second communist state; monasteries were destroyed and monks killed in the 1930s.

events.title: Democratic revolution
events.what: Peaceful hunger strikes and protests brought multiparty democracy without bloodshed.

culture.label: Naadam
culture.text: The summer festival of wrestling, horse racing and archery — the 'three manly games', UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Ger
culture.text: The round felt tent, still lived in by many families and pitched in city suburbs too.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Mutton, dairy and airag — fermented mare's milk, offered to guests and not easily refused.

culture.label: Khöömei
culture.text: Throat singing, producing two notes at once; UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Horses
culture.text: Roughly as many horses as people, and children learn to ride before they can properly walk.

talkAbout: Naadam and the three sports.
Horses and the countryside.
Throat singing and traditional music.
avoid: Genghis Khan is a national hero here, whatever the view elsewhere. Mining's environmental effects and the socialist purges are difficult topics.

people.name: Abai Qunanbaiuly
people.why: The founder of modern Kazakh literature and the country's central intellectual figure.

people.name: Al-Farabi
people.why: Called the Second Teacher after Aristotle; born in Farab, in present-day Kazakhstan.

people.name: Gennady Golovkin
people.why: A long-reigning middleweight world champion and Kazakhstan's biggest sporting name.

people.name: Dinmukhamed Kunaev
people.why: Led Soviet Kazakhstan for 25 years; his dismissal triggered the 1986 protests.

people.name: Dimash Qudaibergen
people.why: A six-octave range that made him a star across Asia and beyond.

events.title: The Kazakh Khanate
events.what: The founding state of the Kazakh people on the steppe.

events.title: The Asharshylyk famine
events.what: Forced collectivisation killed roughly 1.5 million Kazakhs, close to 40% of the population.

events.title: Semipalatinsk
events.what: 456 Soviet nuclear tests were carried out on Kazakh soil, with lasting health consequences.

events.title: Independence
events.what: The last Soviet republic to declare independence, and it gave up the world's fourth-largest nuclear arsenal.

culture.label: Steppe
culture.text: The ninth-largest country in the world, most of it open grassland.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Beshbarmak — 'five fingers' — eaten by hand from a shared platter, plus kumis and shubat.

culture.label: Baikonur
culture.text: Every crewed Soviet and Russian space launch since 1961 has gone from Kazakh soil.

culture.label: Dombra
culture.text: A two-stringed lute; kuy instrumental pieces are the heart of Kazakh music.

culture.label: Hospitality
culture.text: Guests are seated in the place of honour and served the best cut, traditionally the sheep's head.

talkAbout: Horses, the steppe and traditional sports.
Baikonur and the space programme.
Food, and the etiquette of beshbarmak.
avoid: Borat references are genuinely irritating. The famine, the nuclear tests and the 2022 unrest are serious subjects.

people.name: Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani
people.why: Founded Al Jazeera and turned Qatar into a diplomatic and media power.

people.name: Sheikha Al Mayassa
people.why: Widely described as the most powerful person in the art world through Qatar Museums.

people.name: Mutaz Barshim
people.why: Olympic champion who famously agreed to share the 2020 gold rather than jump off for it.

people.name: Sheikha Moza bint Nasser
people.why: Drove the creation of Education City, which hosts branches of several world universities.

people.name: Ali Bin Ali
people.why: Built one of the Gulf's largest trading groups from a family retail business.

events.title: British recognition
events.what: An agreement with Britain recognised the Al Thani as rulers, separating Qatar from Bahrain.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Qatar declined to join the UAE and became independent on its own.

events.title: Al Jazeera launches
events.what: The channel changed Arab media and made Qatar diplomatically consequential.

events.title: The World Cup
events.what: The first World Cup in the Arab world, and the most scrutinised in the tournament's history.

culture.label: Pearling
culture.text: Before gas, Qatar lived on pearl diving; the Museum of Islamic Art sits on the old harbour.

culture.label: Majlis
culture.text: Guests are received with coffee and dates; conversation before business is expected.

culture.label: Falconry
culture.text: The Souq Waqif falcon market and hospital are working institutions, not attractions.

culture.label: Museums
culture.text: Enormous investment in art; the National Museum was designed by Jean Nouvel as a desert rose.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Machboos and thareed; Ramadan iftar tents are a major social occasion.

talkAbout: Falconry and pearling history.
Museums and architecture.
Football, which Qataris follow closely.
avoid: Migrant worker conditions and the World Cup bid are contentious. Politics and the ruling family are not open subjects.

people.name: Jayavarman VII
people.why: Built the Bayon and much of Angkor Thom, and hospitals across the empire.

people.name: Norodom Sihanouk
people.why: Won independence from France and dominated Cambodian politics for six decades.

people.name: Dith Pran
people.why: Survived the Khmer Rouge and coined 'the killing fields'; The Killing Fields tells his story.

people.name: Sinn Sisamouth
people.why: The king of Khmer music, whose 1960s recordings were nearly lost with him under the Khmer Rouge.

people.name: Rithy Panh
people.why: His documentaries on the genocide he survived are among the most important films about it.

events.title: The Khmer Empire
events.what: Angkor was the largest pre-industrial city in the world, with a million people.

events.title: French protectorate
events.what: Nine decades of colonial rule, ending with independence under Sihanouk.

events.title: The Khmer Rouge
events.what: Around 1.7 to 2 million people — a quarter of the population — died from execution, starvation and overwork.

events.title: The UN transition
events.what: One of the UN's largest ever missions organised elections and a new constitution.

culture.label: Angkor Wat
culture.text: The largest religious monument in the world, and the only building on any national flag.

culture.label: Apsara dance
culture.text: Classical Khmer dance was nearly wiped out with its teachers, and was rebuilt from survivors' memories.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Fish amok steamed in banana leaf, kuy teav noodle soup, and prahok fermented fish paste.

culture.label: Sampeah
culture.text: Palms together with the height set by the other person's status, as in Thailand.

culture.label: Water Festival
culture.text: Bon Om Touk, with dragon-boat races on the Tonlé Sap when the river reverses direction.

talkAbout: Angkor and the empire.
Food and the Mekong.
Classical dance and music.
avoid: Nearly every Cambodian family lost people to the Khmer Rouge; let them raise it. Politics is not a safe topic.

people.name: Sirimavo Bandaranaike
people.why: The world's first woman prime minister, in 1960.

people.name: Muttiah Muralitharan
people.why: Took more Test wickets than anyone in history.

people.name: Geoffrey Bawa
people.why: Created tropical modernism, and his buildings shaped how the region builds.

people.name: Michael Ondaatje
people.why: Colombo-born, and author of The English Patient.

people.name: Ananda Coomaraswamy
people.why: Introduced Indian and Sri Lankan art to the West on its own terms.

events.title: Buddhism arrives
events.what: Mahinda brought Buddhism from India; the Sri Maha Bodhi tree at Anuradhapura dates from then.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Ceylon left British rule, becoming the republic of Sri Lanka in 1972.

events.title: The civil war
events.what: Twenty-six years of war between the state and the Tamil Tigers, with heavy civilian losses.

events.title: The tsunami
events.what: The Indian Ocean tsunami killed over 35,000 people along the coast.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Rice and curry with a dozen small dishes, hoppers for breakfast, and startling amounts of chilli.

culture.label: Tea
culture.text: Ceylon tea grown in the hill country is one of the world's great tea traditions.

culture.label: Perahera
culture.text: The Kandy Esala Perahera parades the Buddha's tooth relic with decorated elephants and dancers.

culture.label: Cricket
culture.text: The 1996 World Cup win is a shared national memory.

culture.label: Two languages
culture.text: Sinhala and Tamil are both official, reflecting the island's two main communities.

talkAbout: Food and tea.
Cricket, especially 1996.
Ancient sites — Sigiriya, Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa.
avoid: The civil war and Sinhala–Tamil relations are unresolved and painful. The 2022 economic collapse hit people hard.

people.name: Rumi
people.why: Born in Balkh, in northern Afghanistan; among the most-read poets in the world today.

people.name: Ahmad Shah Durrani
people.why: Founded the Durrani Empire in 1747 and is regarded as the father of modern Afghanistan.

people.name: Khaled Hosseini
people.why: The Kite Runner introduced millions of readers to Afghanistan beyond the news.

people.name: Nadia Anjuman
people.why: Wrote in secret under the first Taliban government; killed at 25.

people.name: Abdul Ghaffar Khan
people.why: Built a non-violent Pashtun movement of 100,000 against British rule; called the Frontier Gandhi.

events.title: Crossroads of empires
events.what: Persian, Greek, Buddhist and Islamic civilisations all passed through; the Bamiyan Buddhas stood for 1,400 years.

events.title: The Anglo-Afghan wars
events.what: Three wars with Britain, which failed to hold the country and recognised its independence in 1919.

events.title: The Soviet war
events.what: A decade of occupation and resistance that killed around a million people and displaced millions more.

events.title: The American war and withdrawal
events.what: Twenty years of intervention ended with the Taliban's return within days of the final withdrawal.

culture.label: Hospitality
culture.text: Pashtunwali makes protecting a guest an absolute obligation; tea is served immediately and repeatedly.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Kabuli pulao with lamb, raisins and carrot is the national dish, served from a communal platter.

culture.label: Carpets
culture.text: Afghan rugs, especially Turkmen and Baluchi designs, are among the finest hand-knotted work anywhere.

culture.label: Kite flying
culture.text: Gudiparan bazi, with glass-coated string, is a serious and skilful contest.

culture.label: Poetry
culture.text: Persian and Pashto poetry are recited widely; Thursday nights at Herat's poetry gatherings are a tradition.

talkAbout: Poetry, which is deeply embedded in everyday speech.
Food and hospitality customs.
Landscape — the Wakhan and Band-e-Amir lakes are extraordinary.
avoid: Politics, the Taliban and women's rights are dangerous subjects for Afghans at home. Many abroad are refugees who have lost a great deal.

people.name: Aung San
people.why: Negotiated independence from Britain and was assassinated six months before it arrived.

people.name: Aung San Suu Kyi
people.why: Nobel Peace Prize winner after fifteen years of house arrest; her later record is heavily contested.

people.name: U Thant
people.why: The first non-European to lead the United Nations, through the Cuban missile crisis.

people.name: Anawrahta
people.why: Founded the Pagan Empire and made Theravada Buddhism the country's faith.

people.name: Ma Thida
people.why: A surgeon jailed as a political prisoner who became a leading writer and free-speech advocate.

events.title: The Pagan Empire
events.what: Over 10,000 temples were built on the plain at Bagan; more than 2,000 still stand.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Burma left British rule, and civil conflict with ethnic armies began almost immediately.

events.title: Military rule
events.what: Half a century of army government, isolation and economic decline.

events.title: The coup
events.what: The military seized power again after an election it lost, triggering a nationwide armed resistance.

culture.label: Buddhism
culture.text: Most young men spend time as novice monks, and the dawn alms round is part of daily life.

culture.label: Thanaka
culture.text: A yellow paste from ground bark worn on the face as sunscreen and decoration.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Mohinga fish noodle soup for breakfast, and laphet — fermented tea leaf eaten as a salad.

culture.label: Longyi
culture.text: A wrapped sarong worn by men and women alike, in offices as well as villages.

culture.label: Thingyan
culture.text: New Year in April, marked with days of water throwing.

talkAbout: Food, especially mohinga and tea leaf salad.
Bagan and the temple plain.
Family and where their township is.
avoid: The coup, the resistance and the Rohingya are all dangerous or painful subjects. Many people abroad are in exile.

people.name: Fa Ngum
people.why: Founded Lan Xang, the kingdom of a million elephants, and unified the Lao lands.

people.name: Kaysone Phomvihane
people.why: Led the Pathet Lao and then the country; his face is on the banknotes.

people.name: Souvanna Phouma
people.why: Repeatedly tried to hold a neutral course through the Indochina wars.

people.name: Anousone Phommachanh
people.why: Part of the generation making Lao pop and hip-hop for a domestic audience.

people.name: Mattie Do
people.why: Laos's first woman feature director, whose horror films have travelled the festival circuit.

events.title: Lan Xang founded
events.what: The kingdom of a million elephants ruled much of the Mekong for three and a half centuries.

events.title: French Indochina
events.what: Laos became a French protectorate, leaving colonial architecture in Luang Prabang and Vientiane.

events.title: The secret war
events.what: The US dropped more than two million tonnes of bombs — the most heavily bombed country per head in history.

events.title: The Lao PDR
events.what: The Pathet Lao took power and abolished the monarchy.

culture.label: Sticky rice
culture.text: Eaten by hand from a woven basket at nearly every meal; Lao people call themselves luk khao niaow, children of sticky rice.

culture.label: Baci
culture.text: A ceremony tying white cotton threads around the wrists to call the soul back and wish well.

culture.label: Luang Prabang
culture.text: A World Heritage town of temples where monks collect alms at sunrise.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Laap, the national dish, and green papaya salad hotter than its Thai cousin.

culture.label: Bo pen nyang
culture.text: 'Never mind, no problem' — an outlook that shapes the pace of everything.

talkAbout: Food, especially laap and sticky rice.
The Mekong and river life.
Festivals like That Luang and the boat races.
avoid: Unexploded bombs still kill people; it is a serious subject, not a curiosity. Politics is not openly discussed.

people.name: Kim Il-sung
people.why: Founded the state in 1948 and remains its 'Eternal President' more than thirty years after his death.

people.name: Kim Jong-il
people.why: Ruled through the famine of the 1990s and built the nuclear programme.

people.name: Han Sorya
people.why: The dominant figure in North Korean literature and its socialist realist style.

people.name: Jong Song-ok
people.why: Won the 1999 world championship marathon, one of the country's few global sporting titles.

people.name: Rim Kum-suk
people.why: Pyongyang's traffic officers became one of the few internationally recognised images of daily life there.

events.title: Division
events.what: Korea was split at the 38th parallel by the US and USSR, intended as a temporary arrangement.

events.title: The Korean War
events.what: Millions died; the armistice has never been replaced by a peace treaty.

events.title: The Arduous March
events.what: A famine after the Soviet collapse killed several hundred thousand to a million people.

events.title: The first nuclear test
events.what: North Korea became a nuclear-armed state, reshaping regional security.

culture.label: Language
culture.text: Korean, with a northern standard that has diverged from the South in vocabulary and loanwords.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Pyongyang naengmyeon — cold buckwheat noodles — is famous across the whole peninsula.

culture.label: Mass Games
culture.text: Tens of thousands of performers producing images with flip-cards in stadium displays.

culture.label: Juche
culture.text: The state ideology of self-reliance, taught in schools and built into public architecture.

culture.label: Divided families
culture.text: Millions of Koreans on both sides have relatives they have never been able to meet.

talkAbout: Korean food and language, which are shared across the peninsula.
The history of the division, which predates either state.
Naengmyeon, which the North is genuinely famous for.
avoid: North Koreans abroad are usually defectors with families still at risk. Never treat the country as a joke or a novelty destination.

people.name: Tawakkol Karman
people.why: Won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2011 for leading Yemen's protest movement; the first Arab woman to win it.

people.name: The Queen of Sheba
people.why: Traditionally associated with the Sabaean kingdom in Yemen, and named in both Bible and Quran.

people.name: Abdullah al-Baradouni
people.why: Blind from childhood, he became Yemen's greatest modern poet and a critic of every government he lived under.

people.name: Nadia Al-Sakkaf
people.why: The first woman to edit a Yemeni newspaper, and later information minister.

people.name: Ali Abdul Aziz Al-Ansi
people.why: One of Yemen's leading contemporary artists, documenting Sanaa's old city.

events.title: The incense kingdoms
events.what: Saba and its neighbours grew rich on frankincense and myrrh, and built the Marib dam.

events.title: The North Yemen civil war
events.what: The imamate fell and a republic was declared after eight years of fighting.

events.title: Unification
events.what: North and South Yemen merged into one republic.

events.title: The war
events.what: Houthi forces took Sanaa; the war that followed created one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

culture.label: Sanaa
culture.text: The old city's tower houses, decorated with white gypsum, have been inhabited for over 2,500 years.

culture.label: Qat
culture.text: Afternoon qat chews are the main social institution, where business and politics are discussed.

culture.label: Jambiya
culture.text: The curved dagger worn at the belt signals a man's tribe and standing.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Saltah with fenugreek froth, and mandi lamb slow-cooked in an underground oven.

culture.label: Socotra
culture.text: An island of dragon's blood trees and species found nowhere else on earth.

talkAbout: Sanaa's architecture and Socotra's wildlife.
Coffee — the word mocha comes from the Yemeni port of Mokha.
Poetry, which is a living popular art here.
avoid: The war has devastated the country and divides Yemenis sharply. Almost everyone has lost someone or been displaced.

people.name: King Hussein
people.why: Reigned 46 years through wars and coup attempts, and made peace with Israel in 1994.

people.name: Queen Rania
people.why: An internationally prominent advocate for education and for a more accurate picture of the Arab world.

people.name: Mustafa Wahbi Al-Tal
people.why: Jordan's national poet, who wrote about ordinary people and was repeatedly jailed for it.

people.name: Ahmad Abughaush
people.why: Won Jordan's first Olympic medal — gold — in 2016.

people.name: Widad Kawar
people.why: Preserved thousands of Palestinian and Jordanian traditional garments that would otherwise be lost.

events.title: Petra
events.what: The Nabataeans carved a trading capital into rose-red sandstone and controlled the incense routes.

events.title: The Arab Revolt
events.what: The revolt against Ottoman rule, in which T. E. Lawrence took part, ran through this territory.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Transjordan became independent from Britain under the Hashemite monarchy.

events.title: Refuge
events.what: Jordan has absorbed successive waves of Palestinian, Iraqi and Syrian refugees; a large share of the population.

culture.label: Mansaf
culture.text: Lamb cooked in fermented dried yoghurt over rice, eaten from a shared tray with the right hand.

culture.label: Wadi Rum
culture.text: A desert of sandstone towers, home to Bedouin communities and a favourite of film crews.

culture.label: Coffee
culture.text: Bitter cardamom coffee poured from a dallah; the host keeps pouring until you shake the cup.

culture.label: Dead Sea
culture.text: The lowest land on earth, and shrinking by about a metre a year.

culture.label: Hospitality
culture.text: Bedouin custom obliges a host to shelter and feed a guest for three days without asking their business.

talkAbout: Petra and Wadi Rum.
Mansaf and coffee etiquette.
Family origins — many Jordanians have Palestinian roots.
avoid: The monarchy, and the balance between Jordanians of Palestinian and East Bank origin, are sensitive. Regional politics is heavy going.

people.name: Fairuz
people.why: The voice of the Arab world's mornings for seventy years, and a symbol of Lebanon itself.

people.name: Khalil Gibran
people.why: The Prophet is one of the best-selling books of all time, in over a hundred languages.

people.name: May Ziadeh
people.why: Ran a Cairo literary salon that shaped Arabic letters, and was a pioneering feminist voice.

people.name: Nadine Labaki
people.why: Capernaum was nominated for an Oscar and made her the Arab world's best-known woman director.

people.name: Amin Maalouf
people.why: Won the Prix Goncourt and sits in the Académie française.

events.title: The Phoenicians
events.what: Tyre, Sidon and Byblos traded across the Mediterranean and spread the alphabet.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Lebanon left French mandate rule with a confessional system dividing power between sects.

events.title: The civil war
events.what: Fifteen years of war killed around 150,000 people and scarred Beirut.

events.title: The port explosion
events.what: One of the largest non-nuclear explosions ever recorded destroyed much of Beirut and killed over 200 people.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Mezze in profusion, tabbouleh that is mostly parsley, and manakish for breakfast.

culture.label: Music
culture.text: Fairuz in the morning is close to a national ritual; the pop and indie scenes are strong too.

culture.label: Landscape
culture.text: You can ski and swim in the same day; the cedar is on the flag.

culture.label: Trilingual
culture.text: Arabic, French and English mixed within single sentences.

culture.label: Diaspora
culture.text: Far more people of Lebanese descent live abroad than in Lebanon itself.

talkAbout: Food, which Lebanese will argue about with real conviction.
Music, film and nightlife.
The diaspora and family abroad.
avoid: Sectarian politics, Hezbollah, Syria and Israel are all charged. The 2020 explosion and the economic collapse are raw.

people.name: Hammurabi
people.why: His law code, carved on a stele, is among the earliest written legal systems.

people.name: Zaha Hadid
people.why: Baghdad-born, the first woman to win the Pritzker Prize, and one of the century's defining architects.

people.name: Al-Mutanabbi
people.why: Often called the greatest poet in the Arabic language; Baghdad's book street is named for him.

people.name: Nazik Al-Malaika
people.why: Broke Arabic poetry out of its classical metres and started the free verse movement.

people.name: Nadia Murad
people.why: A Yazidi survivor of ISIS captivity who won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2018.

events.title: Writing invented
events.what: Cuneiform appeared in Sumer, in southern Iraq — the beginning of recorded history.

events.title: Baghdad and the House of Wisdom
events.what: The Abbasid capital was the largest city on earth and the centre of world scholarship.

events.title: Saddam Hussein
events.what: Two wars, the gassing of Halabja, and a sanctions decade that hollowed out the country.

events.title: The invasion
events.what: The US-led invasion removed Saddam and set off years of insurgency and sectarian war.

culture.label: Mesopotamia
culture.text: Writing, the wheel, the city and the law all have their earliest known forms here.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Masgouf grilled river fish, dolma, and biryani unlike the South Asian version.

culture.label: Books
culture.text: 'Cairo writes, Beirut publishes, Baghdad reads' is an old saying Iraqis still quote.

culture.label: Chaikhana
culture.text: Tea houses where men sit for hours over small glasses and backgammon.

culture.label: Diversity
culture.text: Shia and Sunni Arabs, Kurds, Turkmen, Assyrian Christians, Yazidis and Mandaeans.

talkAbout: Ancient history — Iraqis are proud of Mesopotamia and tired of being defined by recent war.
Poetry and books.
Food, especially masgouf.
avoid: Sectarian politics, the invasion and ISIS are all difficult. Nearly every family has been displaced or bereaved.

people.name: Sultan Qaboos bin Said
people.why: Transformed Oman from near-medieval isolation into a modern state over fifty years.

people.name: Ahmad bin Majid
people.why: The Lion of the Sea, whose navigation manuals guided Indian Ocean sailing for centuries.

people.name: Yusuf Al Sirani
people.why: Part of the generation that made Oman a competitive side in Gulf football.

people.name: Jokha Alharthi
people.why: Celestial Bodies won the International Booker Prize in 2019, the first Arabic novel to do so.

people.name: Said bin Sultan
people.why: Ruled an empire from Zanzibar, making Oman a major Indian Ocean power.

events.title: Expelling the Portuguese
events.what: Oman drove Portugal from Muscat and built a maritime empire reaching to East Africa.

events.title: The capital moves to Zanzibar
events.what: For a time the sultan governed his empire from an island off Africa.

events.title: The Renaissance
events.what: Qaboos deposed his father and began building schools, hospitals and roads where there were almost none.

events.title: Quiet diplomacy
events.what: Oman's neutrality made it the venue for the secret talks behind the Iran nuclear deal.

culture.label: Seafaring
culture.text: A long Indian Ocean tradition, with dhow building still practised at Sur.

culture.label: Aflaj
culture.text: Ancient gravity-fed irrigation channels, some 2,000 years old and still in use; UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Frankincense
culture.text: The Dhofar region produces some of the finest frankincense in the world.

culture.label: Dress
culture.text: The dishdasha with a tassel, and either a kuma cap or a wrapped massar turban.

culture.label: Ibadi Islam
culture.text: Oman is the only Ibadi-majority country, a school known for tolerance and moderation.

talkAbout: Frankincense and the Dhofar mountains.
Seafaring history and the Zanzibar connection.
Wadis, forts and the mountains — Oman has around 500 forts.
avoid: Politics and the ruling family are not discussed. Don't lump Oman in with its Gulf neighbours; Omanis see themselves as distinct.

people.name: Sheikh Mubarak Al-Sabah
people.why: Called Mubarak the Great, he secured Kuwait's autonomy and founded the modern state.

people.name: Abdullah Al-Salem
people.why: Oversaw independence and the 1962 constitution, one of the Gulf's most liberal.

people.name: Suad Al-Sabah
people.why: A member of the ruling family who became a leading Arabic poet and publisher.

people.name: Laila Al-Othman
people.why: One of the Gulf's most prominent women writers, prosecuted for her work and undeterred.

people.name: Fahad Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah
people.why: Played for the national team and was killed defending Dasman Palace during the invasion.

events.title: Kuwait founded
events.what: A small settlement grew into a pearling and trading port at the head of the Gulf.

events.title: Oil at Burgan
events.what: One of the largest oil fields ever found transformed the country within a generation.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Kuwait ended its treaty with Britain and adopted a constitution and elected parliament.

events.title: The Iraqi invasion
events.what: Seven months of occupation, then liberation; retreating troops set 700 oil wells alight.

culture.label: Diwaniya
culture.text: Evening gatherings in a dedicated room where men discuss politics and business; central to Kuwaiti public life.

culture.label: Parliament
culture.text: The Gulf's most assertive elected assembly, which regularly forces ministers out.

culture.label: Pearling
culture.text: Before oil, Kuwait's dhows dived for pearls; the sea and boat-building remain central to identity.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Machboos with dried lime, and gers ogaily saffron cake.

culture.label: Kuwait Towers
culture.text: The 1979 water towers are the city's emblem and were shelled in the occupation.

talkAbout: The diwaniya tradition and how it works.
Pearling and maritime history.
Food and family gatherings.
avoid: The 1990 invasion is a national trauma. Stateless bidoon residents and migrant labour conditions are politically sensitive.

people.name: Timur
people.why: Built an empire from Samarkand and is the central figure of modern Uzbek national identity.

people.name: Ulugh Beg
people.why: Timur's grandson built an observatory at Samarkand and produced star tables of remarkable accuracy.

people.name: Al-Khwarizmi
people.why: Gave us algebra and, through the Latin form of his name, the word algorithm.

people.name: Avicenna
people.why: The Canon of Medicine was Europe's standard medical text for six centuries.

people.name: Alisher Navoi
people.why: Proved Turkic could be a literary language equal to Persian, and founded Uzbek literature.

events.title: The Silk Road
events.what: Samarkand, Bukhara and Khiva were the great caravan cities between China and the Mediterranean.

events.title: The Timurid Renaissance
events.what: Samarkand became a centre of astronomy, architecture and miniature painting.

events.title: The Aral Sea
events.what: Soviet cotton irrigation drained what had been the world's fourth-largest lake.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Uzbekistan left the Soviet Union, and has opened up considerably since 2016.

culture.label: Plov
culture.text: Rice with lamb, carrot and cumin, cooked in a kazan; there is a national plov centre in Tashkent.

culture.label: Registan
culture.text: Three madrasas facing a square in Samarkand, covered in blue tilework.

culture.label: Non
culture.text: Stamped round bread, never placed upside down, and torn rather than cut.

culture.label: Chaikhana
culture.text: Tea houses where the first cup is poured back into the pot three times before serving.

culture.label: Suzani
culture.text: Large embroidered hangings, traditionally made for a bride by her family.

talkAbout: Plov, and how each region makes it differently.
The Silk Road cities.
Bread and tea customs.
avoid: The Karimov years, forced cotton labour and the Aral Sea disaster are difficult. Politics remains sensitive.

people.name: Magtymguly Pyragy
people.why: The national poet, who helped forge a Turkmen literary language and identity.

people.name: Saparmurat Niyazov
people.why: Ruled as Türkmenbaşy with an extreme personality cult, renaming months after his family.

people.name: Gurbansoltan Eje
people.why: Niyazov's mother, killed in the Ashgabat earthquake and later made a national symbol.

people.name: Berdi Kerbabaev
people.why: The founder of modern Turkmen prose and a major figure in Soviet Central Asian literature.

people.name: Nury Halmammedov
people.why: Blended Turkmen folk music with classical form; his film scores are still widely loved.

events.title: Nisa and the Parthians
events.what: The Parthian Empire's early capital, now a World Heritage site outside Ashgabat.

events.title: Geok Tepe
events.what: Russian forces stormed the Turkmen fortress; the date is now a day of remembrance.

events.title: The Ashgabat earthquake
events.what: Destroyed the city and killed a large share of its population.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Turkmenistan left the USSR and declared permanent neutrality, recognised by the UN in 1995.

culture.label: Carpets
culture.text: Turkmen carpet designs are on the national flag, and each tribe has its own gul motif.

culture.label: Akhal-Teke
culture.text: The 'golden horse', with a metallic sheen to its coat; one appears on the national emblem.

culture.label: Darvaza
culture.text: The Door to Hell — a gas crater that has been burning since the 1970s.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Çorba soup, plov, and bread baked in a tamdyr clay oven.

culture.label: Ashgabat
culture.text: Rebuilt in white marble, and holder of a Guinness record for the most marble-clad buildings.

talkAbout: Carpets and their tribal patterns.
Akhal-Teke horses.
The Silk Road cities of Merv and Konye-Urgench.
avoid: Turkmenistan is one of the most closed countries in the world; politics is genuinely dangerous to discuss. Personality-cult jokes are unwise.

people.name: Chinghiz Aitmatov
people.why: The most widely translated Central Asian writer, and a national figure in his lifetime.

people.name: Kurmanjan Datka
people.why: The 'Queen of the South', who negotiated with the Russian Empire to protect her people.

people.name: Roza Otunbayeva
people.why: Central Asia's first woman head of state, who handed over power voluntarily.

people.name: Sayakbay Karalaev
people.why: Could recite the half-million-line Manas epic from memory; the greatest of its bards.

people.name: Aisuluu Tynybekova
people.why: World champion and Olympic medallist, and one of Kyrgyzstan's biggest sporting names.

events.title: The Epic of Manas
events.what: An oral epic twenty times longer than the Odyssey, still performed by trained bards.

events.title: The Urkun
events.what: A revolt against Russian conscription was crushed; tens of thousands died fleeing to China.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Kyrgyzstan left the Soviet Union and became the region's most politically open state.

events.title: Two revolutions
events.what: Popular uprisings removed two presidents, earning the country a reputation for turbulent democracy.

culture.label: Yurt
culture.text: The shanyrak roof-ring is on the national flag, and yurts are still used in summer pastures.

culture.label: Mountains
culture.text: Over 90% of the country is mountainous; Lake Issyk-Kul is the second-largest alpine lake in the world.

culture.label: Kok-boru
culture.text: Horseback game played with a goat carcass; the national sport and fiercely contested.

culture.label: Kymyz
culture.text: Fermented mare's milk, drunk in summer at the high pastures.

culture.label: Eagle hunting
culture.text: Berkutchi hunt with golden eagles, a tradition shared with Kazakh and Mongol herders.

talkAbout: The Manas epic and its bards.
Mountains, jailoo pastures and trekking.
Eagle hunting and horse games.
avoid: Bride kidnapping is a real and criminalised problem, not folklore. Ethnic tension in the south around Osh is sensitive.

people.name: Shota Rustaveli
people.why: The Knight in the Panther's Skin is the national epic, once part of every bride's dowry.

people.name: Queen Tamar
people.why: Ruled Georgia's golden age and is still called 'King' Tamar in Georgian.

people.name: Niko Pirosmani
people.why: A self-taught sign painter who died in poverty and is now Georgia's most loved artist.

people.name: Katie Melua
people.why: Georgian-born, and one of Britain's best-selling artists of the 2000s.

people.name: Lasha Talakhadze
people.why: Holds every super-heavyweight world record and is the strongest lifter in history.

events.title: The birth of wine
events.what: The oldest known winemaking, in clay qvevri buried in the ground — still done that way.

events.title: Christianity adopted
events.what: Georgia became one of the first states in the world to make Christianity its religion.

events.title: Didgori
events.what: David the Builder's victory over a far larger Seljuk army opened Georgia's golden age.

events.title: The war with Russia
events.what: A five-day war left South Ossetia and Abkhazia outside Georgian control.

culture.label: Wine
culture.text: Eight thousand years of it, fermented in buried clay vessels; UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Supra
culture.text: A feast led by a tamada who gives long, structured toasts; refusing to drink to them is difficult.

culture.label: Polyphony
culture.text: Three-part singing found nowhere else in quite this form; UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Khinkali dumplings held by the twisted top, and khachapuri bread filled with cheese and egg.

culture.label: Alphabet
culture.text: Georgian has its own script, unrelated to any other, in three historical forms.

talkAbout: Wine and the supra.
Polyphonic singing.
Mountains — Svaneti and Kazbegi are extraordinary.
avoid: Russia, and the status of Abkhazia and South Ossetia, are raw. Don't confuse Georgia with the US state.

people.name: Mesrop Mashtots
people.why: Created the Armenian alphabet in 405, which preserved the language through centuries without a state.

people.name: Aram Khachaturian
people.why: The Sabre Dance and the Spartacus ballet made him one of the Soviet Union's great composers.

people.name: Charles Aznavour
people.why: Sold over 180 million records and was France's most famous Armenian.

people.name: Komitas
people.why: Collected thousands of Armenian folk songs; the genocide broke him and he never composed again.

people.name: Viktor Hambardzumyan
people.why: A founder of theoretical astrophysics who built the Byurakan Observatory.

events.title: The first Christian state
events.what: Armenia adopted Christianity as its state religion before anyone else.

events.title: The alphabet
events.what: Mashtots's script let Armenian survive centuries of foreign rule.

events.title: The genocide
events.what: Around 1.5 million Armenians were killed by the Ottoman state; recognition is still contested.

events.title: The Velvet Revolution
events.what: Weeks of peaceful protest brought down the government without a shot.

culture.label: Khachkars
culture.text: Intricately carved stone crosses, no two alike; UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Lavash
culture.text: Thin bread baked on the wall of a tonir oven; also UNESCO-listed.

culture.label: Duduk
culture.text: An apricot-wood double reed with a sound heard in film scores worldwide.

culture.label: Apricots
culture.text: The scientific name for the apricot means 'Armenian plum', and the flag's orange band is said to reflect it.

culture.label: Diaspora
culture.text: Far more Armenians live abroad than in Armenia, in Russia, the US, France and the Middle East.

talkAbout: The alphabet and language.
Music, especially the duduk.
Food, brandy and family connections abroad.
avoid: The genocide, and its denial, are central. Nagorno-Karabakh and relations with Azerbaijan and Turkey are acutely painful.

people.name: Jigme Singye Wangchuck
people.why: Coined Gross National Happiness and then voluntarily handed power to a democracy.

people.name: Ngawang Namgyal
people.why: Unified Bhutan, built its dzong fortresses and gave it its legal code.

people.name: Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck
people.why: The Dragon King, who has overseen Bhutan's democratic and environmental commitments.

people.name: Kunzang Choden
people.why: The first Bhutanese woman to publish a novel in English.

people.name: Karma Ura
people.why: Built the Gross National Happiness index into something that could actually be measured.

events.title: Unification
events.what: The Zhabdrung unified the valleys and built the dzongs that still serve as administrative centres.

events.title: The monarchy founded
events.what: Ugyen Wangchuck became the first Druk Gyalpo, ending centuries of internal conflict.

events.title: Gross National Happiness
events.what: Bhutan declared it would measure development by wellbeing rather than output.

events.title: Democracy
events.what: The king gave up absolute power and Bhutan held its first parliamentary elections.

culture.label: Carbon negative
culture.text: The constitution requires 60% forest cover; Bhutan absorbs more carbon than it emits.

culture.label: Archery
culture.text: The national sport, played at long range with singing, dancing and heavy teasing of opponents.

culture.label: Dress
culture.text: The gho and kira are worn to work, school and official business by law.

culture.label: Ema datshi
culture.text: Chillies and cheese — the national dish treats chilli as a vegetable, not a spice.

culture.label: Tiger's Nest
culture.text: Paro Taktsang clings to a cliff 900 m above the valley floor.

talkAbout: Gross National Happiness and how it is measured.
Archery matches and festivals.
The forests and carbon commitment.
avoid: The expulsion of Lhotshampa (Nepali-speaking) Bhutanese in the 1990s is a serious and largely unacknowledged issue.

people.name: Nizami Ganjavi
people.why: His Khamsa of five epic poems is among the greatest works in Persian literature.

people.name: Uzeyir Hajibeyov
people.why: Wrote the first opera in the Islamic world, fusing mugham with Western form.

people.name: Garry Kasparov
people.why: Baku-born, world champion for fifteen years and the man who played Deep Blue.

people.name: Lev Landau
people.why: Baku-born Nobel laureate whose textbooks trained generations of physicists.

people.name: Zeynalabdin Taghiyev
people.why: Funded the Muslim world's first secular school for girls, in 1901.

events.title: The first oil well
events.what: Baku drilled what is often called the world's first industrial oil well, decades before Pennsylvania.

events.title: The first secular Muslim republic
events.what: The Azerbaijan Democratic Republic gave women the vote before Britain or the United States did.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Azerbaijan left the Soviet Union as the Karabakh conflict was already under way.

events.title: Nagorno-Karabakh
events.what: Azerbaijan retook the territory; the Armenian population left almost entirely in 2023.

culture.label: Land of Fire
culture.text: Natural gas seeps burn at Yanar Dag, and Zoroastrian fire temples predate Islam here.

culture.label: Tea
culture.text: Served in armudu pear-shaped glasses with jam rather than sugar.

culture.label: Mugham
culture.text: Improvised modal music with poetry, UNESCO-listed and taken very seriously.

culture.label: Plov
culture.text: Dozens of varieties, often served with a saffron crust and dried fruit.

culture.label: Carpets
culture.text: Azerbaijani weaving has distinct regional schools and its own museum shaped like a rolled rug.

talkAbout: Tea culture and mugham music.
Baku's old city and its oil-boom architecture.
Food, especially plov and dolma.
avoid: Nagorno-Karabakh and Armenia are the defining national conflict. Domestic politics and press freedom are sensitive.

people.name: Isa bin Salman Al Khalifa
people.why: Led Bahrain to independence in 1971 and through its first decades as a state.

people.name: Ebrahim Al-Arrayedh
people.why: A founding figure of modern Bahraini and Gulf poetry.

people.name: Ruqaya Al Ghasra
people.why: Competed at the Olympics in a hijab and full body suit, and won her heat in 2008.

people.name: Nancy Khedouri
people.why: A member of Bahrain's small Jewish community appointed to its parliament's upper house.

people.name: Mohammed bin Mubarak Al Khalifa
people.why: Bahrain's first foreign minister and a long-serving deputy prime minister.

events.title: Dilmun
events.what: A trading civilisation the Sumerians described as a paradise; its burial mounds are World Heritage-listed.

events.title: The Al Khalifa arrive
events.what: The family that still rules Bahrain took the islands from Persian control.

events.title: First oil in the Gulf
events.what: Bahrain struck oil before any of its neighbours, and ran out first too.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Bahrain became independent from Britain rather than joining the UAE.

culture.label: Pearls
culture.text: Bahraini natural pearls were the finest in the world; cultured pearls are banned to protect them.

culture.label: Date palms
culture.text: The Tree of Life stands alone in the desert, fed by an unknown water source.

culture.label: Formula One
culture.text: Bahrain hosted the first Grand Prix in the Middle East, in 2004.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Machboos and muhammar sweet rice, plus a strong fish tradition.

culture.label: Mixed society
culture.text: Shia and Sunni Muslims, plus long-established Christian, Jewish and Hindu communities.

talkAbout: Pearl diving history and the Dilmun mounds.
Formula One.
Food and the fish markets.
avoid: The 2011 protests, sectarian politics and the ruling family are all sensitive subjects.

people.name: Hassanal Bolkiah
people.why: One of the longest-reigning monarchs in the world, on the throne since 1967.

people.name: Bolkiah
people.why: The fifth sultan, under whom Brunei's empire reached across Borneo and into the Philippines.

people.name: Omar Ali Saifuddien III
people.why: The architect of modern Brunei, who negotiated independence from Britain.

people.name: Yura Halim
people.why: Wrote the national anthem and served as a senior minister.

people.name: Faiq Bolkiah
people.why: A member of the royal family who has played professional football abroad.

events.title: The Bruneian Empire
events.what: Brunei controlled much of Borneo and parts of the Philippines from its river capital.

events.title: British protectorate
events.what: Brunei accepted British protection after losing territory to Sarawak's white rajahs.

events.title: Oil at Seria
events.what: The discovery that made Brunei one of the wealthiest states in Asia.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Brunei became fully independent, retaining an absolute monarchy.

culture.label: Kampong Ayer
culture.text: A water village on stilts inhabited for over 1,300 years, with schools, mosques and a fire station.

culture.label: Islam
culture.text: Malay Islamic Monarchy is the state philosophy; Friday prayers close businesses.

culture.label: Rainforest
culture.text: Around 70% primary rainforest — the best-preserved in Borneo.

culture.label: Ambuyat
culture.text: A sago starch eaten with bamboo forks, dipped in sour sauce and swallowed without chewing.

culture.label: No alcohol
culture.text: Sales are banned; non-Muslims may import a limited personal quantity.

talkAbout: Kampong Ayer and its history.
The rainforest and Ulu Temburong.
Ambuyat and how to eat it.
avoid: Criticism of the sultan is prohibited. The sharia penal code has drawn international objection and is not casual conversation.

people.name: Mohamed Thakurufaanu
people.why: Drove out the Portuguese after fifteen years of occupation; the national hero.

people.name: Mohamed Nasheed
people.why: The Maldives' first democratically elected president; held a cabinet meeting underwater to publicise sea-level rise.

people.name: Ibrahim Nasir
people.why: Led the country to independence in 1965 and started its tourism industry.

people.name: Hussain Salaahuddin
people.why: A major figure in Dhivehi literature and education.

people.name: Mariyam Waheeda
people.why: One of the first Maldivian women to compete internationally in athletics.

events.title: Conversion to Islam
events.what: The Buddhist kingdom converted, and the Maldives has been Muslim ever since.

events.title: Independence
events.what: The Maldives left British protection after 78 years.

events.title: The tsunami
events.what: Waves washed over most of the country; a third of the population was directly affected.

events.title: The underwater cabinet
events.what: Ministers in scuba gear signed a climate declaration on the seabed to make a point the world would notice.

culture.label: Elevation
culture.text: The lowest country on earth, averaging about 1.5 m above sea level across 1,190 islands.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Tuna in everything: mas huni for breakfast, garudhiya broth, and fish curry.

culture.label: Bodu beru
culture.text: 'Big drum' music and dance, performed by a group with a lead singer and building tempo.

culture.label: Dhoni
culture.text: The traditional wooden boat, still the main way between islands.

culture.label: One island, one resort
culture.text: Tourism is deliberately separated from local islands, which most visitors never see.

talkAbout: Island life away from the resorts.
Bodu beru drumming.
Fishing, which is the traditional backbone of the economy.
avoid: It is a conservative Muslim country; alcohol and public dress rules apply outside resorts. Politics has been turbulent and is sensitive.

people.name: Zenobia
people.why: Ruled Palmyra and challenged Rome across the eastern Mediterranean before being captured.

people.name: Adonis
people.why: The most influential living Arabic poet, and a perennial Nobel candidate.

people.name: Nizar Qabbani
people.why: A diplomat whose love poems and political verse are known by heart across the Arab world.

people.name: Fateh Al-Moudarres
people.why: The founder of modern Syrian art, drawing on Mesopotamian and Byzantine imagery.

people.name: Ghiath Matar
people.why: Handed roses and water to soldiers during the early protests; tortured to death at 26.

events.title: Ugarit and the alphabet
events.what: One of the earliest alphabets was written in cuneiform on the Syrian coast.

events.title: The Umayyad Caliphate
events.what: Damascus ruled an empire from Spain to India; the Umayyad Mosque still stands.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Syria became independent from France after twenty-six years of mandate rule.

events.title: The war and the fall of Assad
events.what: Protests became a war that killed hundreds of thousands and displaced half the country; Assad fell in December 2024.

culture.label: Damascus
culture.text: Among the oldest continuously inhabited cities on earth, and once the centre of an empire.

culture.label: Food
culture.text: Aleppo's cooking is legendary — kibbeh in dozens of forms, muhammara, and cherry kebab.

culture.label: Aleppo soap
culture.text: Olive oil and laurel soap, aged for months, made the same way for centuries.

culture.label: Diversity
culture.text: Sunni and Alawite Muslims, Christians of several churches, Druze, Kurds, Armenians and Assyrians.

culture.label: Hospitality
culture.text: Famous even by regional standards; refusing food takes real persistence.

talkAbout: Food, especially Aleppo's, which Syrians are proud of.
Poetry and music.
Ancient history — Palmyra, Bosra and the Damascus old city.
avoid: Almost every Syrian has lost people or their home. Politics is dangerous and divisive; let them lead.

people.name: Ang Lee
people.why: The first non-white director to win the Academy Award for Best Director, twice.

people.name: Tsai Ing-wen
people.why: Taiwan's first woman president, in office 2016–2024.

people.name: Morris Chang
people.why: Founded TSMC, which makes most of the world's most advanced chips.

people.name: Audrey Tang
people.why: A civic hacker who became a minister and reshaped how Taiwan does open government.

people.name: Teresa Teng
people.why: Her voice was so popular across Chinese-speaking Asia that a saying went 'Deng rules by day, Teng by night'.

events.title: Dutch Formosa
events.what: The Dutch East India Company ruled the south before being expelled by Koxinga.

events.title: Japanese rule
events.what: Fifty years that built railways, schools and much of the island's infrastructure.

events.title: The 228 Incident
events.what: A crackdown killing thousands, followed by 38 years of martial law — the longest in the world at the time.

events.title: The first direct election
events.what: Taiwan completed its transition to democracy with a directly elected president.

culture.label: Night markets
culture.text: The centre of social life: stinky tofu, oyster omelettes, beef noodle soup and games.

culture.label: Bubble tea
culture.text: Invented in Taiwan in the 1980s and now sold on every continent.

culture.label: Temples
culture.text: Folk religion is vivid and everywhere; the Mazu pilgrimage draws millions over nine days.

culture.label: Indigenous peoples
culture.text: Sixteen recognised Austronesian peoples, whose ancestors' languages spread across the Pacific.

culture.label: First in Asia
culture.text: Taiwan legalised same-sex marriage in 2019, the first place in Asia to do so.

talkAbout: Night markets and food, which Taiwanese take enormous pride in.
Hiking — the island is very mountainous.
Film, music and the democratic transition.
avoid: Taiwan's status is the most sensitive question in East Asian politics, and Taiwanese views on it differ widely. Ask rather than assume.

people.name: Rudaki
people.why: The father of Persian poetry, born in what is now Tajikistan.

people.name: Ismail Samani
people.why: Founder of the Samanid empire, claimed as the founder of the Tajik nation; the currency is named for him.

people.name: Sadriddin Ayni
people.why: The founder of modern Tajik literature.

people.name: Bobojon Ghafurov
people.why: His history The Tajiks shaped how the nation understands its own origins.

people.name: Manizha
people.why: Tajik-born, she performed at Eurovision with a song about Russian women's lives.

events.title: The Samanid Empire
events.what: A Persian revival centred on Bukhara and Samarkand that Tajiks trace their identity to.

events.title: A Soviet republic
events.what: Tajikistan was separated from Uzbekistan and made a full Soviet republic, without Samarkand or Bukhara.

events.title: Independence
events.what: Tajikistan left the USSR and slid into civil war within months.

events.title: The civil war
events.what: A regional and ideological war killed tens of thousands and displaced over a million.

culture.label: The Pamirs
culture.text: The Roof of the World; over 90% of the country is mountainous and half is above 3,000 m.

culture.label: Osh
culture.text: The Tajik plov, eaten from a shared dish; the national dish and the centre of every gathering.

culture.label: Navruz
culture.text: The Persian new year is the biggest holiday of the year, with sumalak cooked overnight.

culture.label: Language
culture.text: Tajik is Persian written in Cyrillic — mutually intelligible with Iranian and Afghan Persian.

culture.label: Atlas silk
culture.text: Bright ikat-dyed fabric worn as everyday dress by women.

talkAbout: The Pamir highway and mountain travel.
Persian poetry, which Tajiks share with Iran and Afghanistan.
Navruz and its foods.
avoid: The civil war and current politics are sensitive. Many Tajik men work in Russia and the separation is a hardship.

people.name: Xanana Gusmão
people.why: Led the guerrilla resistance, was imprisoned in Jakarta, and became the country's first president.

people.name: José Ramos-Horta
people.why: Won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1996 for two decades of campaigning in exile.

people.name: Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo
people.why: Shared the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize for defending Timorese civilians under occupation.

people.name: Nicolau Lobato
people.why: The first commander of the armed resistance, killed by Indonesian forces; the airport carries his name.

people.name: Maria Madeira
people.why: The first Timorese artist to exhibit at the Venice Biennale.

events.title: Portuguese Timor
events.what: Four and a half centuries of Portuguese rule left Catholicism and the Portuguese language.

events.title: The invasion
events.what: Nine days after independence was declared, Indonesia invaded.

events.title: The Santa Cruz massacre
events.what: Soldiers fired on a funeral procession in Dili; footage smuggled out changed international opinion.

events.title: Independence
events.what: After a UN-run referendum and transition, Timor-Leste became the first new country of the 21st century.

culture.label: Tais
culture.text: Handwoven cloth given at ceremonies and worn as a marker of region and family.

culture.label: Uma lulik
culture.text: Sacred houses that hold a clan's heirlooms and organise its ritual life.

culture.label: Catholicism
culture.text: Among the most Catholic countries in the world; the church sheltered people during the occupation.

culture.label: Coffee
culture.text: Organic arabica grown in the highlands is the main non-oil export.

culture.label: Languages
culture.text: Tetum and Portuguese are official, Indonesian and English are working languages, and there are around 30 more.

talkAbout: Coffee and the highlands.
Tais weaving and its meanings.
Diving — the reefs off Atauro are among the richest recorded.
avoid: The occupation killed perhaps a quarter of the population; almost every family lost someone. Relations with Indonesia are complicated.
